page: Microsoft Azure L96aos_v5 is a storage-optimized virtual machine hosted on Microsoft Hyper-V architecture. Based on the x86_64 AMD processor platform, the instance provides 96 dedicated vCPUs paired with 768 GB of system memory, establishing an 8 GB per vCPU allocation ratio. The hardware configuration does not feature discrete GPU accelerators.

The defining characteristic of the L96aos_v5 is its direct-attached local storage footprint, which integrates 69,111 GB of local NVMe SSD capacity. The instance also supports Azure Premium Storage for persistent managed disks. Network allocations do not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses, aligning with isolated cloud network topologies.

By consolidating massive local NVMe capacity with high memory density, this instance limits the performance overhead associated with remote block storage. Tradeoffs involve managing node-level ephemeral storage lifecycles against persistent requirements. The resource configuration directly fits I/O-intensive workloads, including large distributed NoSQL databases, transactional engines, data warehousing, and big data analytics pipelines.
description: Microsoft Azure L96aos_v5 is a storage-optimized virtual machine designed for high-throughput, data-intensive enterprise workloads. Driven by an x86_64 AMD processor running under Microsoft Hyper-V, the system delivers 96 dedicated vCPUs alongside 768 GB of RAM, sustaining an 8 GB per vCPU resource ratio. Its primary differentiator is an integrated 69,111 GB local NVMe SSD array, complemented by Premium Storage compatibility for external disks. The instance operates without discrete GPU accelerators and provisions zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, emphasizing secure internal network topologies. By co-locating massive high-speed NVMe flash with substantial memory capacity on a single node, the L96aos_v5 minimizes I/O bottlenecks and disk attachment overhead. This architecture offers qualitative operational efficiency for high-capacity distributed databases, big data analytics engines, data warehousing, and transactional NoSQL workloads requiring rapid local read and write operations.
